Accused in S.C.No.84/2023 pending before the Court of III Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Raichur, arising out of Crime No.56/2023 registered by Balaganoor police station, Raichur for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302 and 504 of IPC is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. seeking regular bail.

Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.56/2023 was registered by Balaganoor police station, Raichur against the petitioner herein for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 302 of IPC on the basis of the first information dated 04.05.2023 received from Parvati, who is the mother of the deceased.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner was arrested on 04.05.2023.
The investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302 and NC: 2024:KHC-K:3513 504 of IPC.
The bail application filed by the petitioner before the Trial Court in S.C.No.84/2023 was rejected on 04.11.2023.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the petitioner, who has no criminal antecedents is in custody for the last more than one year.
He submits that the statement of the alleged eyewitness is unnatural.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has opposed the petition.
He submits that the first informant had spoken to the deceased just prior to the date of alleged incident.
He also submits that CW.3 - Bhagyamma is an eyewitness to the incident in question.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
6. The material on record would go to show that the marriage of the petitioner with deceased Usha was a love marriage.
The petitioner and Usha had married about 4 to 5 months prior to the date of alleged incident, in NC: 2024:KHC-K:3513 Vaishnavi temple at Sindhanur.
Since the marriage was against the wishes of the parents of Usha, her parents had not attended the marriage.

It is alleged Reddeppa @ Reddappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146449285/
2 that after marriage, the petitioner was suspecting the character of his wife and therefore, he was harassing and assaulting her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 03.05.2023 at about 4.30 p.m. Usha allegedly had spoken to the first informant over mobile phone belonging to the petitioner herein and had informed the first informant that she was assaulted by the petitioner.
Therefore, the first informant and her relatives immediately came to the spot of the incident and found the dead body of Usha, which had injuries.
The first informant was allegedly informed by CW.3 - Bhagyamma at about 03.30 p.m. that she had seen the petitioner assaulting Usha with a wooden piece.

Though the first informant was informed by the alleged eyewitness on 03.05.2023 at about 5.00 p.m. about the petitioner assaulting Usha and committing her murder, the first informant had approached the police only on 04.05.2023.
Therefore, I find some force in the arguments addressed NC: 2024:KHC-K:3513 by learned counsel for the petitioner that the statement made by the alleged eyewitness Bhagyamma appears to be false.
Be that as it may, the fact remains that investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
The petitioner is in custody from 04.05.2023.
Under the circumstances, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that petitioner's prayer is required to be considered affirmatively.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
